coverage: median over the datasets of the share of clones with ≥ 2 cells that the tool represents; a run that failed, stopped or could not start because too few clones reach the tool's minimum size counts as 0. Datasets outside a tool's scope (LARRY barcodes for Benisse, which needs receptor sequences) and runs the authors cancelled are left out. Better or worse: more than 5 percentage points from Threadfin.
two_cell: the same for clones of exactly two cells.
datasets: datasets on which the tool produced a result, of those within its scope (the same rule as above).
traits: measured annotations that no tool used (sorting gates, isotype, mutation, tissue, time, later fate; RNA-derived calls excluded), each scored on the clones the tool represents: the tool is better (worse) on an annotation when the 95 % paired bootstrap interval (10,000 resamples) of R² − R²(Threadfin) excludes 0; an interval end within the Monte-Carlo error of 0 is unresolved and not counted. Column verdict: two-sided sign test of better vs worse annotations, P < 0.05.
traits_disjoint: as above, but the representation and the annotation come from disjoint halves of each clone's cells, and the tool's R² is compared with Threadfin's on the same halves and the same clones (3 random splits, both directions, averaged; Clonotrace and Benisse: split 0 only); sign test over annotations.
reid: share of clones whose representation from one half of their cells is nearest to their own other half, compared with Threadfin on the same halves and clones (median over datasets of the mean over splits); Wilcoxon signed-rank test over datasets. With fewer than 6 datasets no paired test can reach P < 0.05, so the tile is descriptive.
fate: LARRY: mean reciprocal rank (ties counted as mid-ranks) of each day-4 clone's own day-6 clone among all day-6 clones; 95 % paired bootstrap interval over clones (10,000 resamples).
sim_groups: simulated data with a known answer: share of each clone's 10 nearest clones that follow its planted programme (mean over clones), compared with Threadfin on the same clones; the unit is the simulation seed (the two donor-shift levels and the two clone-size regimes of a seed share clones or donors, so their differences are averaged within the seed); Wilcoxon signed-rank test over seeds. 10 seeds for every tool except Clonotrace (3 seeds: descriptive, since no paired test of 3 seeds can reach P < 0.05).
sim_mixed: AUROC for telling clones made of two kinds of cells from clones of cells halfway between them (clones ≥ 10 cells), tested over seeds as above.
time: time to compute the clone representation, divided by Threadfin's on the same dataset (median); Clonotrace: only runs whose clone distances used several R sessions, a run stopped at 72 h counted as 72 h. Better or worse: every ratio beyond 25 % in the same direction, otherwise a Wilcoxon test on the log ratios (descriptive with fewer than 6 datasets).
memory: peak memory, the same way. For Clonotrace /usr/bin/time sees only the main R session, so the job's peak from the scheduler is used where the run had a job of its own, and the main session otherwise (a lower bound, marked ≥).
cores: time with 1 core divided by time with 16 cores (GSE287123 RBD). The scopes differ: Threadfin's complete analysis, the other tools' clone representation. Better or worse: more than 25 % from Threadfin's gain.
growth: how much longer the clone representation takes for 10 times more clones, from 5-50 % subsets of GSE195673 (8 cores; exponent of a fit to 4 subsets). Better or worse: an exponent more than 0.25 from Threadfin's.
finished: runs on the full data and on the disjoint halves that finished with the tool's default settings; failed or stopped runs, and runs that needed a larger cell graph, are counted against the tool. Inputs with fewer clones than a tool can represent at all (clone2vec: 11 clones of ≥ 3 cells; Clonotrace: 3 of its minimum size) and runs the authors cancelled are not counted.
tally: number of tiles of the row that are better and worse than Threadfin. The columns are not independent questions, so the count is a summary of the row, not a score or a ranking.
